probe.method: GET, read-only; three sequential requests, 10-second client timeout
probe.limitations: No server restart, process instrumentation, route-specific trace, or upstream timing breakdown was performed.

source_findings.finding: Cold summary construction streams the complete order_intents CSV, counts 132,247 rows in the live response, and retains rolling audit_rows/last_rows using list append plus pop(0).
The same synchronous build then loads local state, fetches an exchange account snapshot, and appends exchange history before composing the response.
The pinned source has a 2-second in-process cache; the cache lock protects only cache lookup/update, not the expensive build. Warm requests were fast in this probe.

diagnosis: The measured cold request took 6.223s, then cache-hit requests took 0.102s and 0.084s. The handler's likely dominant work is the unbounded full-history CSV scan and synchronous downstream snapshot/state reads; the available probe does not isolate their individual durations, so attribution to one specific blocking read is not proven. The initial task report of timeout may reflect cold-build latency exceeding the caller's 3-8s timeout. Response size is ~5.65 MB.
change: No source change made. The live endpoint returned HTTP 200 for all probes and its pinned code already has a cache. A code change to truncate or async-ify audit/history would alter payload semantics and would require broader validation; no safe bounded fix was established from the available read-only evidence.
safety: Live process PID 8668 was not restarted, killed, or reconfigured. Ports 8014 and 8000 were not touched. Certification matrix and apply_verified_results.py were not touched.
